second_order: putting together an April Fools Trek trivia theme
theme_note: The request, supplied quotations, playful fake answer, referrals, and thanks are turns in one shared practice: helping assemble the weekly trivia game's April Fools material; what varies is whether people retrieve, invent, redirect, or acknowledge an answer.

second_order: posting TNG in the Place without a surviving plan
theme_note: This single surviving title gestures toward TNG participation in Place, but its deleted body leaves no other practice with which it can responsibly be grouped.

second_order: calling Trekkies to build Star Trek on the canvas
theme_note: These codes publicly recruit the room to make a Star Trek image or take a Star Trek target; the proposed object varies across Starfleet, communicators, Spock, Enterprise, and a comm badge on another image.

second_order: removing image posts and directing text resubmission
theme_note: The community's moderation tool applies the same image-post rule to event submissions and tells posters how to resubmit; later instances vary only in the image and thread.

second_order: sharing links, coordinates, pictures, and guides for the builds
theme_note: These codes turn a general call into something helpers can locate or follow by supplying a bitmap, coordinates, direct links, pictures, guides, borders, or a destination subreddit.

second_order: asking what r/place is while others call it spam or nonsense
theme_note: These turns contest or explain the event's place in the room: some demand an explanation, one supplies it, and others dismiss the posts or the effort; the variation is between incomprehension, explanation, and rejection.

second_order: playing along with r/startrek being owned by CBS
theme_note: Moderators and participants jointly sustain the CBS/All Access fiction, including the Scott Bakula AMA: moderators sell flair, delay releases, invoke lawyers and marketing, while participants test, recognize, praise, question, and play along with the premise.

second_order: asking to keep and archive the April Fools ship
theme_note: These codes concern preserving, finding, praising, closing, and archiving the subreddit's own changed ship/banner after the joke, rather than performing the CBS ownership fiction itself.

second_order: asking others to screw with Garrett Wang on Twitter
theme_note: This single call recruits the room into an off-platform April Fools prank and belongs with no other practice in the pooled codes.

second_order: reporting what Star Trek made and what later died
theme_note: These codes claim success, representation, progress, completion, or death for the room's canvas work; reports range from 'we did it' through progress and final images to 'dead, Jim.'

second_order: protecting, repairing, and filling in the builds
theme_note: Participants describe the repeated maintenance work that keeps images present: protecting for hours, adding colour, repairing borders and middles, and rebuilding against vandals.

second_order: posting and recognizing fake Discovery news
theme_note: A fake casting post and a bait teaser use Discovery news as an April Fools prank; the two codes vary between publishing the bait and knowingly clicking it.

second_order: trying to make Broccoli the first image result
theme_note: This one-code practice uses upvotes for a separate April Fools image-result prank and belongs with nothing else.

second_order: working around neighbours who occupy the pixels
theme_note: These codes adjust Star Trek work to other people on the canvas through peace, truces, warnings, relocation, avoiding damage, or reporting takeover; what varies is whether the encounter produces accommodation, retreat, or loss.

second_order: trying to get organised through targets, allies, and Discord
theme_note: The codes work through the practical problem of too few people by weighing alternative targets, imagining alliances, asking for Discord, downloading it, and later using it for art and maintenance bots.

second_order: arguing which comm badge to make
theme_note: One participant asks why the TNG badge was chosen and another states a preference while suggesting the other badge be organised elsewhere; the exchange is a distinct choice about the image.

second_order: consolidating a ton of help requests into one post
theme_note: This single moderator action gathers accumulated requests and announces removal of further help threads; it is neither another recruitment call nor ordinary image-post enforcement.
